subject: Production latency spike impacting Ingestify — SLA apportionment request
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@ingestify.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Production latency spike impacting Ingestify — request for SLA apportionment

Hi Laura / Marissa,

We observed a sharp p95 latency spike across our ingestion endpoints last night (01:28–02:03 UTC on 2026-11-20). Our PagerDuty and synthetic checks both flagged a ~35 minute window where ~18% of requests saw >2s p95 and error rates remained low but latency-heavy — effectively a partial degradation.

Our network team traced the root cause to a third-party peering provider (TransPort Peering East) that reported packet loss on the 01:20–02:00 UTC window. From our side we saw most of the affected traffic exit through the east peering fabric.

We need Redwood's apportionment calculation per the SLA: specifically whether this counts as an excusable third-party outage, and if not, how uptime credits would be allocated for the affected hour. We have attached our edge metrics CSV and can share PCAPs if helpful.

Attachments: ingestify_edge_metrics_20261120.csv

Please advise next steps and what logs you need from us. This incident impacts a live job run for several customers and we need a resolution and, if applicable, credit calculation for procurement.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
Head of Platform Reliability
Ingestify

---
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@ingestify.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike impacting Ingestify — request for SLA apportionment

Tom — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the edge metrics CSV. We’re pulling logs now and coordinating with network/ops to validate routing and any possible mitigation we could have applied (e.g., automatic egress reroute).

Two quick asks that will speed the apportionment review:
- Can you confirm whether the majority of affected requests used the east peering fabric (region-east) or if you saw similar traces via region-west?
- If possible, please share a sample request-id or two from the 01:28–01:40 UTC window so we can correlate with our request logs.

We treat third-party network incidents as potentially excusable per Section 5.3 of the SLA, but we still run an apportionment process (we evaluate whether Redwood had reasonable reroute capability and whether mitigation was possible). If we determine partial responsibility we’ll propose a proportional credit.

I’ll loop in Marcus (infrastructure) and Marissa (CS) to keep procurement and credits in the loop.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Laura — quick follow-up with the traces you requested.

We confirm affected traffic was routed via the east peering fabric. Sample request ids: req_8f3a2b, req_8f3a4c (timestamps 01:33:21 UTC and 01:35:09 UTC). Our support bundle includes the CSV (attached) and a small PCAP we can upload to a secure transfer if you need it.

We understand there are clauses for third-party network providers but from our perspective this produced a measurable partial-degradation that should be reflected in uptime calculations. Please confirm whether Redwood will:
- Run an internal replay/correlation for those request ids and share the matching server-side logs, and
- Produce an apportionment worksheet showing the methodology used to calculate any credit (we need this for our procurement team).

We’ve created an internal ticket (Support#7842) — happy to hop on a call if that helps.

Thanks,
Tom

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@ingestify.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-22T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike impacting Ingestify — request for SLA apportionment

Tom — thanks for the samples and for the CSV. We completed our internal correlation and wanted to share the preliminary apportionment and next steps.

Summary of findings:
- Event window observed by Redwood: 2026-11-20 01:28:00–02:03:00 UTC.
- Percentage of total regional requests impacted (Redwood logs correlated with your request ids): ~15.7% of requests from region-east saw >2s p95 within that window.
- Causal attribution: TransPort Peering East reported packet loss impacting their ASN; however, our edge telemetry shows transient queuing and elevated retransmits that persisted for ~22 minutes even after TransPort's packet-loss window began to clear.

SLA interpretation and proposed apportionment:
- Section 5.3 allows exclusion for third-party network outages where customer traffic was routed through a third-party provider and Redwood had no reasonable technical mitigation. That said, our ops team determined we had partial mitigation opportunity (e.g., dynamic egress reroute from the affected POP to an adjacent POP) but it would have caused additional request path changes and possible cache misses with real risk to consistency for Ingestify's multi-tenant workload.
- Given the above, our recommendation is 60% Redwood responsibility for the degraded minutes and 40% third-party responsibility. Applying the SLA credit formula (apportioned by affected minutes and percent responsibility) results in a proposed credit equivalent to a 0.30 day SLA credit against the monthly invoice for the impacted billing period.

Attachments and evidence provided:
- ingestify_edge_logs_20261120.tar.gz (server logs correlated to req_8f3a2b and req_8f3a4c)
- apportionment_calc_ingestify_20261122.xlsx (detailed calculation and time-series) — hosted here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d_apportionment_calc

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether the proposed 0.30 day credit is acceptable to Ingestify procurement. If accepted, we will issue a credit against invoice INV-202611 or process via a DocuSign acknowledgment depending on your procurement preferences.
2) If you would like a technical readout/call, Marcus and Rishi are available tomorrow morning to walk through the telemetry and reroute options we considered.

I’ll keep this thread as the single source of record for the apportionment. If you need us to redact any PII from the logs before sharing internally, let me know.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
